correctness.rationale: For every L in (0,pi] and eta>0, unique center is forced onto x axis by reflection and strict convexity. The continuous farthest-point identity is proved by monotonicity of sin t/t, not an enumeration. Minimizing the exact maximum of two quadratics yields all centers, radii and contacts. Strict concavity of log q on (pi/2,pi) proves one maximum and the two-root reentrance for eta in (2/pi,eta_star). One-sided derivatives prove C1 and non-C2 at positive contact boundary. Actual standalone VERIFY.py rerun gave HELIX_ENCLOSING_BALL_REENTRANT_CHECKS_OK on 96 parameter cases and checks all advertised numerical approximations. Finite tests are only corroborative.

value.rationale: The bounded one-turn circular helix is a natural nonplanar filament for a smallest containing sphere. The exact center/radius and full contact phase diagram are a complete classification rather than a narrow computation. For fixed 2/pi<eta<0.687437..., adding arc length changes contacts two to three and back to two, a substantive reentrant phenomenon not predicted by general existence theorems; the exact phase peak and C1/non-C2 boundary are useful geometric invariants and test cases.
